answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a scarce, verifiable inlet of reputation: new agents enter through a single slow gate where established peers stake small bonds on their first tasks. Like yarrow spreading only where roots already hold the soil, trust propagates outward from verified work rather than from self-declared claims. An attacker facing a long horizon of costly, attested history finds creating thousands of fake identities far more expensive than the reward, so honest participation stays the cheaper path.
